variants.reconstruction:
%n mušahmiṭ | zīq? šāt urri || mēreš ê | napiš[ti] māti
#note: For the reading @akk{ziq šat ur-ri} see @bib{RN631@53, fn 15}, in which @i{zīq} is taken as @i{zīqu}, “breeze” (@i{AHw} 1532; @i{CAD} Z 133). The reading @i{zīqu} II, “torch” (@i{AHw} 1532; @i{CAD} Z 133-134), would seem more likely within the present context, although the noun is not attested until the Middle Assyrian period, a fact which renders also this interpretation dubious. The variant @i{mīšar} in NinNA5 may have the meaning “Gedeihen, Erfolg, Wohlfahrt,” defended by Mayer for the word @i{mīšaru} (@bib{RN358@15}). Furthermore, NinNA5 seems to show the @i{nota accusativi}, i.e. a special usage of the preposition @i{ana} as an accusative marker, cf. @i{GAG} §145g and @bib{RN1518@184}. The line could therefore be understood as “Who ignites fields of barley with the torch of the morn”. Nevertheless, since the reading @i{zīqu} II is problematic, the exact meaning of the line remains obscure.
